checks: Each attached primary PDF was checksum-verified where retrieved from storage and swept once for methods, results, every results table, and usable figures.
Population layouts use the strongest directly reported axis; pooled/shared values are retained on the first applicable row only.
Tabs 1-4 are staged for every paper; Tabs 5-10 are staged only where the primary PDF directly supports a value or where the permitted transparent aggregation/percentage-to-count rule applies.
No exposure, count, burden, or incidence value was back-calculated from another metric. Transparent sums and percentage-derived counts are identified in the individual notes.
All staged field IDs were checked against the local extraction schema and every structured value will be dual-written through population sync.

papers.note: Batch 021 manual primary-PDF extraction using GPT-5.6 Sol (medium; GPT-5.5 unavailable). Methods, results, and Tables 1-4 were checked (article pp. 1-9); no compatible result figure was present. Match / Training is the directly reported setting split. The primary headline uses the source's medical-attention injury counts and rates; separate time-loss counts/rates, days and burden are retained. Total exposure 8772.25 h is the transparent sum of the directly reported 271.25 match and 8501 training hours, not a rate back-calculation. Structured location and tissue rows are time-loss values from Tables 2-4; direct and indirect opponent-contact counts are transparently summed in the contact field. The source prints a likely erroneous training ligament/joint-capsule CI (1.41 [0.03-0.85]); it is preserved verbatim for reviewer attention. The global seven re-injuries and all illness outcomes remain on the first row only because no setting split was reported for them.

papers.note: Batch 021 manual primary-PDF extraction using GPT-5.6 Sol (medium; GPT-5.5 unavailable). Abstract, methods, results, Tables 1-3, and Figure 1 were checked (article pp. e248-e253). The directly reported COVID-19-negative / COVID-19-positive comparison is the population layout. All injuries are time-loss injuries; Table 2 provides group-specific player-hours, counts and incidence with CIs, and Table 3 provides the compatible type, location, contact, severity, and match/training counts. Injury-type categories were not mutually exclusive. Directly mappable structured rows were retained; dislocation/subluxation and combined hip/groin and lower-back/pelvis/sacrum categories were not forced into narrower schema fields. This single MLS Next academy cohort is retained as processing, not american_data: it is neither High School RIO, NCAA, nor national US surveillance.

Artificial turf / Natural grass is the direct surface-comparison layout. All outcomes are match injuries, so the per-surface total and match exposures are both retained. Table 2 supplies direct counts, incidence with 95% CIs, recurrence, contact, severity, tissue and location rows; Table 3 supplies position rows. Injury information is missing for some source events, and overuse injuries were excluded by the study.

papers.note: Batch 021 manual primary-PDF extraction using GPT-5.6 Sol (medium; GPT-5.5 unavailable). Abstract, methods, results, Tables 1-3, and Figures 1-6 were checked (article pp. 1-28). Injured / Non-injured is the directly selected case-comparison layout (20 players each). The paper directly reports 20 non-contact time-loss injury cases, no repeat injuries, and a study-specific usable injury rate of 4.5 per 1000 h, but not raw total exposure; no exposure was calculated. The reported overall rate is therefore retained on the first row only. The four source muscle-group percentages (hamstring 35%, quadriceps 25%, adductors 25%, gastrocnemius 15%) use the stable 20-injury numerator: permitted percentage-to-count mapping gives thigh 17 and lower leg 3, and their transparent sum gives 20 muscle injuries. Figures and Tables 1-3 concern ACWR prediction/model performance and add no other schema-compatible injury outcome values. The selected injured/non-injured case-control framing and small sample warrant reviewer attention.
